what_its_for: Lansoprazole is used to reduce the amount of acid your stomach makes. It is used to treat heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), stomach ulcers, and a condition called erosive esophagitis (irritation of the food pipe caused by acid). It can also be used to treat conditions where the stomach makes too much acid, such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
how_to_take: Take lansoprazole by mouth, usually once a day in the morning, at least 30 minutes BEFORE a meal. Swallow capsules whole — do not crush or chew them. If you have trouble swallowing a capsule, you can open it and sprinkle the tiny granules onto a tablespoon of applesauce, yogurt, or cottage cheese and swallow right away without chewing. For orally disintegrating tablets (SoluTab), place the tablet on your tongue and let it dissolve — do not chew it. You can also dissolve the SoluTab in a small amount of water and swallow it.
dosing: Your doctor will tell you the right dose for you. Common adult doses are 15 mg to 30 mg once daily. Some conditions may require higher doses or twice-daily dosing. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly. Do not take more or less than prescribed. For over-the-counter (OTC) use for frequent heartburn, the usual dose is 15 mg once daily for 14 days. Do not use OTC lansoprazole for more than 14 days unless directed by your doctor.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still before your next meal. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store lansoprazole at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking lansoprazole with certain medications without asking your doctor first, including blood thinners like warfarin, HIV medications like atazanavir or nelfinavir, antifungal medicines like ketoconazole, or methotrexate. Avoid alcohol and spicy or fatty foods, as these can worsen acid reflux. Do not take antacids right before or after taking lansoprazole unless your doctor says it is okay. Avoid taking it with sucralfate — if you need both, take lansoprazole at least 30 minutes before sucralfate.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe stomach pain, diarrhea that is watery or bloody (this could be a sign of a serious gut infection), signs of low magnesium such as muscle cramps, irregular heartbeat, or seizures, signs of vitamin B12 deficiency such as unusual tiredness or tingling in hands and feet (with long-term use), bone pain or unusual fractures (with long-term use), signs of lupus such as a rash on your cheeks or arms that worsens in sunlight, signs of serious kidney problems such as decreased urination or swelling in legs, or a severe allergic reaction including rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve after several weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to feel relief from heartburn within 1 to 4 days of starting lansoprazole, but it may take 1 to 4 weeks of regular use to feel the full benefit. For healing of ulcers or erosive esophagitis, it may take 4 to 8 weeks. Do not stop taking it early just because you feel better — continue for the full course your doctor has prescribed.
special_populations: Older adults (65+): Lansoprazole is generally safe for older adults, but long-term use may increase the risk of bone fractures, low magnesium, and vitamin B12 deficiency. Talk to your doctor about monitoring. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using lansoprazole if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. Breastfeeding: It is not fully known if lansoprazole passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medication. Children: Lansoprazole can be used in children as young as 1 year old for certain conditions, but the dose is based on weight. Always follow your child's doctor's instructions. Liver problems: If you have liver disease, your doctor may need to lower your dose, as the medication stays in your body longer.
